content.thinking:
This intervention frames climate scientists as helping communities prepare for extreme weather through early-warning systems, which highlights benevolence and competence in a practical, non-political way that should resonate across partisan lines. It also touches on scientists collaborating with policymakers and emergency managers, which could bump up perceptions of policy involvement.

Since this is really about weather forecasting rather than climate belief directly, I'd expect belief in human-caused climate change to shift only marginally, maybe +0.3-0.6. Funding perceptions could rise modestly given the positive framing of NOAA, NASA, and NWS work, especially relevant amid current cuts to these agencies. Naming these institutions explicitly should give institutional trust a stronger boost than most other arms, and overall multidimensional trust looks like a solid +2.3-2.8 given the strong benevolence/competence framing.

Working through the rest of the metrics: policy role around +1.8 given the emphasis on scientists collaborating with forecasters and planners, funding around +1.3, concern around +0.9 due to the extreme weather framing, and behavior staying low around +0.4 since this is adaptation-focused rather than mitigation-focused. I'm also noting that since this text centers on meteorology, the AMS donation item could see an outsized boost — maybe +$0.11 — compared to other arms, with newsletter signup around +0.008.

Its mechanism is 'scientists are useful, caring, and working with the people who protect you' — non-accusatory, apolitical, and hence unlikely to trigger partisan reactance, so I expect above-average movement on the fresh multidimensional trust battery (especially benevolence/competence) at roughly +2.5 points, with the pre-anchored single-item trust moving less (~+1.6) and distrust falling modestly.
